body.text: r1: d anvayam āpādayati / pratiṣedhaniṣedhasya vidhānarūpatvāt* / asataḥ sapakṣān na nivṛttir ity asapakṣa eva nāstīti cet* / neti saiva nivṛtter nirvṛttiḥ asataḥ katham iṣṭā / abhāvapratiṣedho hi bhāvo
body.translated_text: r1: [This objection] brings about a positive concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>); because a denial of a negation has the form of a positive injunction. [Objection:] If [it is claimed that] from the non-existent there is no exclusion from the <s>sapakṣa</s> (similar instances), so there simply are no <s>asapakṣa</s> (dissimilar instances) — [we reply:] Not so; for that very [claim] is the non-arising of exclusion. How could the non-existent be desired [as a basis]? For indeed a negation of an absence is a positive entity

body.text: 2: 'saty apy asti / bhāvapratiṣedhas tu na saṃbhavatīty askhalitaprajño devānāṃpriyo yas tadviṣayaṃ pratiṣedhaṃ necchati / asad abhāva iti ca vyavaharati / nirloṭhitaś cāyam artho 'sati nāstitety
body.translated_text: 2: even when [the positive entity] exists, it exists; but a negation of a positive entity is not possible — thus [says] the foolish <s>devānāmpriya</s> (dear to the gods, i.e., a simpleton) who does not want a negation directed at that object. And one conventionally uses the expression 'the non-existent is an absence.' This matter has been thoroughly analyzed — 'of the non-existent there is no non-existence' [applies]

body.text: 3: arthāntare / tena neha pratanyate / na cāsann ātmā sattāsādhanavṛtteḥ sandigdhaḥ syāt* / na ca pareṇa tathopagata iti // apramāṇād abhyupagamāt tathaiva bhavati / atiprasaṅgāt* /
body.translated_text: 3: to a different meaning. Therefore it is not elaborated here. Nor should the self (<s>ātman</s>) as non-existent be doubtful with respect to the operation of means of establishing existence; nor has it been accepted as such by the opponent. [Response:] It follows in exactly that way from acceptance on the basis of an invalid means of knowledge (<s>apramāṇa</s>), [for] the reason of being over-extended (<s>atiprasaṅga</s>).

body.text: 4: na copagamabalena sapakṣāsapakṣau vyavasthāpya pramāṇapravartanaṃ yuktam* / evaṃ hy āgamasiddha ātmā syāt* / nānumānasiddhaḥ / tasmād avyatireke 'py asataḥ / sapakṣād vyatirekaḥ sandigdhaḥ
body.translated_text: 4: Nor is it reasonable, having established <s>sapakṣa</s> and <s>asapakṣa</s> by the force of mere acceptance, to proceed with a means of valid knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>); for in this way the self would be established by scripture (<s>āgama</s>) alone, not by inference (<s>anumāna</s>). Therefore, even in the absence of deviation [from the subject], for the non-existent — the deviation from the <s>sapakṣa</s> would be doubtful

body.text: 5: syāt* prāṇādīnāṃ / ātmanaḥ sandehāt* / ata eva vipakṣād api / ekatra hi niyame siddhe 'nyanivartanaṃ
body.translated_text: 5: in the case of [vital functions like] <s>prāṇa</s> and the rest, on account of the doubtfulness of the self. For the very same reason [it would be doubtful] also regarding the <s>vipakṣa</s> (dissimilar instances); for when invariable concomitance in one case is established, the exclusion of others

body.text: v1: sidhyet* / anyathā kvacid dṛṣṭe 'bhāvasidhāv api syād evādṛṣṭe saṃśayaḥ / tathā hy asakalavyaktibhedavyāpino 'py arthāḥ kecit tajjātisaṃbhavino dṛṣṭāḥ pārthivālohalekhyavat* / virodhasya cādṛṣṭeḥ saṃdeha
body.translated_text: v1: would be proved; otherwise, even in a case where absence has been proved through something seen [somewhere], there would be doubt regarding the unseen. For indeed, some properties, though not pervading all individual distinctions, are seen as arising from that [common] class — as [in the case of] things made of earth, iron, and lacquer. And regarding the non-perception of contradiction, [there would be] doubt

body.text: 2: eva / nairātmyena prāṇādīnāṃ uktalakṣaṇasya virodhasyāsiddheḥ / sandigdho nairātmyād vyatirekaḥ / ātmapratiniyame hi tatkāryātmatayā prāṇādīnāṃ nairātmyena saha virodhaḥ
body.translated_text: 2: only; because of the non-establishment of the contradiction, characterized as stated, of <s>prāṇa</s> etc. with the absence-of-self (<s>nairātmya</s>). The deviation [of the inference] from the absence-of-self is doubtful. For a contradiction between <s>prāṇa</s> etc. and the absence-of-self would [only] arise if there were an essential connection (<s>nairātmya</s>) to the self-regulated causation of [the self's] effects

body.text: 3: syāt* / sa ca na sidhyatīty uktam* / astu nāma nirātmakebhyo vyatirekaḥ prāṇādīnāṃ tadbhāve ca nairātmyavyāvṛttiḥ / tathāpi nānairātmyād ātmā jīvaccharīre sidhyati / yenāyaṃ na vyatirekasyābhāvaṃ
body.translated_text: 3: but that, as has been said, is not established. Even granting that there is deviation of <s>prāṇa</s> etc. from what lacks a self, and that the absence-of-self is excluded when that [self] exists — even so, the self is not proved in a living body by means of non-absence-of-self; that is why [the opponent] does not want absence of the deviation

body.text: 4: bhāvam icchati / yathā vyatirekābhave 'pi sapakṣe prāṇādir neṣṭaḥ / sapakṣāvyatirekī ced dhetur hetur ato 'nvayī / nānvayavyatirekī ced anairātmyaṃ na sātmakaṃ / iti saṃgrahaślokaḥ /
body.translated_text: 4: to be present [as proof]. Just as even in the absence of deviation in the <s>sapakṣa</s>, <s>prāṇa</s> etc. are not desired. If the reason is non-deviating from the <s>sapakṣa</s>, it is a reason [only] through positive concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>); if it is not [a reason] through both positive and negative concomitance, then the absence-of-self (<s>nairātmya</s>) is not [the mark of what] has a self. This is a summary verse.

body.text: 5: na prāṇādisaṃbhavena nairātmyavyāvartanād ātmagati / kiṃ tarhi vidhimukhenaiva prāṇādayaḥ
body.translated_text: 5: The self is not established by the exclusion of the absence-of-self through the arising of <s>prāṇa</s> etc.; rather, it is [established] precisely through a positive [approach] — what then? [That] <s>prāṇa</s> etc. [are established]
